scope: Three untried mechanisms only. PR #60 already tried signed paired throw; its cached in-sample proxy and optimistic status have been retired. The literal registry gate stops all new candidate construction.
ranking_basis: Qualitative expected information gain for new-fault discrimination per implementation cost; not a numerical prediction of DTI improvement.
novelty_scope: Compared with checked-in H86 and merged SPT source, not an exhaustive claim against every public or private sibling raster. Scientific novelty does not imply competition uniqueness.

hypotheses.name: Cross-fault magnetic marker translation
hypotheses.signature: For label-free candidate line orientations, phase-correlate magnetic texture on opposite flanks. Require an along-line translation of transverse magnetic markers, consistent in adjacent windows, and a weaker zero-shift match. Keep both signed slip directions rather than assuming one regional sense of slip.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A buried shear zone may truncate and displace a pre-existing magnetic marker even without a mapped surface trace. Searching the image rather than extrapolating catalogue tips makes this capable in principle of finding off-catalogue structures.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: GFCO compares TMI with upward-continued TMI and constructs visible-tip/relay priors; GMC compares gradients between different physical fields. Neither estimates along-fault displacement of transverse markers in two flanks of the same magnetic image. The concurrently merged WVB lane uses local-wavenumber/depth concordance and fault-valve coupling, not flank-to-flank along-fault marker translation.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted intrusive contacts with unrelated texture; acquisition-block seams and remanent magnetization changes.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Highest qualitative priority, very uncertain; no measured gain or score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: oriented flank extraction, bounded phase correlation, uncertainty and seam controls.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: the raw mirrored core can be restored, but the required shared cached stack is not present. Do not rebuild a substitute under this protocol.
hypotheses.date_scope: Re-reviewed 2026-10-24 after merged SPT trial; still untested

hypotheses.name: Basement–gravity forward-residual displacement
hypotheses.signature: Fit a spatially cross-fitted, low-frequency forward gravity response of basement depth using only training-region rock-density priors. Test line-like *residual* changes in its signed transverse gradient that persist when the physical model is refitted without the test block; compare against unmodeled raw gravity edges and same-sign paired steps.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A buried displaced interface can leave a localized gravity misfit even when an exposed scarp or mapped surface trace is absent; a catalogue-independent residual test can search covered basins rather than extrapolating known tips.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: H86-RMRB regressed radiometric K~Th+U against RTP, not a gravity forward-response residual. PR #60 SPT intersected raw signed basement/gravity flank steps using the full-catalogue collar; this instead asks whether a cross-fitted physical forward model fails locally and does not reuse its trial as a novel method.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Variation in basin-fill density, inverse-model artifacts and igneous contacts; if the basement depth was derived from the same gravity measurements, the residual is circular and cannot be interpreted as independent confirmation.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Second qualitative information opportunity if independent provenance is confirmed; no numeric forecast or holdout score.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: verify inversion lineage and units, physically constrained forward model, spatial refits, residual/seam and density-null controls.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: must establish whether basement depth was inverted from this gravity band and restore actual shared cached features; if input independence is impossible, retire before testing.

hypotheses.name: Watershed-crossing scarp persistence
hypotheses.signature: Measure signed scarp steps that retain strike and down-side polarity across independently delineated drainage divides. Reject candidates that only follow a channel, constant-elevation shoreline, road bench, or one alluvial fan boundary.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A small tectonic scarp may be missed in regional mapping; persistence across unrelated catchments is evidence beyond a single ridge or lineament.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: GFCO uses scarplet collinearity, piedmont hinges, valley chains and relief deconfounding. It does not condition the signed step on independent watershed topology across divides. WVB uses relief-normalized scarps and shoreline controls, not independently delineated watershed topology.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Paleolake shorelines, fluvial terraces and road cuts. Drainage divides alone cannot distinguish these from a fault.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Third qualitative priority; physically useful discriminant but expensive and geographically incomplete until DEM coverage is verified. No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: native-resolution DEM acquisition, hydrologic conditioning, catchments and raster aggregation.
hypotheses.free_official_source_needed: USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM products referenced by the competition's 1m_DEM_links.csv, not a resampled 100 m proxy.
hypotheses.obtainability: Official metadata and the competition description were retrieved through the page-fetch service on 2026-10-23. Neither the authenticated CSV nor the required native DEM tiles were acquired here. Metadata reachability is not data obtainability.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: no native DEM bytes, license-specific product manifest, complete coverage audit, or shared cached watershed stack. Not offered as a runnable experiment.

required_validation_after_blockers_are_r: Assign one method lane; restore and hash-verify the actual shared cached feature stack and a current complete accessible registry.
Preserve the literal rho and overlap limits; do not exempt a dense prior without an explicitly revised protocol.
Freeze buffered whole-component folds and fixed budgets before using withheld labels. Derive every catalogue feature only from fold-visible faults.
Feature-alone and combined canaries precede any trusted result. AUC above 0.90 stops the run; include constant, shuffled and polarity-scrambled controls.

Use the pinned shared evaluate_holdout.py and submission_writer.py. Report pooled HOLDOUT-DTI with evaluator hashes, withheld-positive count, physical-block 95% CI and paired delta against the strongest rerunnable matched control.
Do not compare maxima from different fold designs as a current holdout best. A positive paired result and all uniqueness gates are required before separate slot selection.
At most three experiments or two hours; a negative result is a deliverable. No organizer submission is authorized by this plan.
